title: The cost of boxing in a loop

questions.stem: What does this page say is wrong with `Integer sum = 0; for (int i = 0; i < 1000000; i++) { sum += i; }`?

options.text: Nothing costly: the compiler keeps `sum` as a plain `int` in the loop
options.says: The page says this loop creates a new Integer object again and again, which is slow.

options.text: Every pass boxes `i` into an `Integer` before comparing it to the limit
options.says: The page's loop declares i as an int; the boxing it describes is of the running total.

options.text: Every `+=` unboxes the total and boxes a fresh `Integer` for the result
options.says: The page says each iteration involves auto-boxing and unboxing of the Integer total.
